reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling spans three linked facilities in Northern Virginia with 44 MW of IT capacity. Assuming 40 kW per rack, a standard density for AI training clusters, this translates to roughly 1,100 racks. The campus occupies 420,000 square feet, yielding approximately 2.6 MW per 10,000 square feet, a moderate density suggesting mixed workload support rather than optimization for high-density accelerator deployment.

The facility holds certifications for financial services compliance, health data security, federal contracting, and infrastructure resilience. It ranks 12th by published capacity among Virginia's 25 facilities with disclosed megawattage, representing 2.7% of the state's published 1,603 MW. Of Virginia's 330 mapped data center locations, only 25 publish power figures, placing Sterling among the disclosed minority.

Sterling's capacity is material but not exceptional for AI infrastructure. At 44 MW, the campus could support a modest model training pipeline or mid-scale inference deployment but lacks the scale of purpose-built AI campuses approaching or exceeding 100 MW. Its relevance depends on whether CyrusOne's grid interconnection and power procurement at this site can sustain expansion or whether Virginia's grid constraints limit its role in large-scale AI scaling.
